article.title: Genitivo vs acusativo bajo negación
article.chapter: Acusativo y animacidad — Винительный падеж и одушевлённость

claims.summary: Under negation, Russian allows alternation between accusative and genitive in the nominal group functioning as object. The choice is not merely formal and interacts with definiteness, quantification, negation scope, lexical meaning of the verb, and speaker's presentation of the referent.

In affirmative sentences, the object is in accusative (e.g., Я читаю книгу). With negation, the accusative can remain (Я не читаю эту книгу) when referring to a specific referent. Genitive can appear when negation implies absence, zero quantity, lack of realization, or an undetermined referent (Я не читаю книг). The choice also depends on lexical and stylistic trends.

Examples illustrate the alternation between accusative and genitive under negation, such as 'Он не прочитал письмо' (He didn't read the letter) and 'Он не получил письма' (He didn't receive a letter). The article also shows how genitive is used for negated existential constructions like 'Нет времени' (There is no time).
